audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 4 and 6 disagreed with their own why text: whys[3] 'she out-trades my poke' and whys[4] 'her spike, not mine' sat under a stored Skill, and whys[6] 'my DoT deletes a one-blink squishy' sat under a stored Aurora.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Lillia and the why lines match it exactly. The packet also flags the chart as contradicting the 60% win rate — that reads as a late-game champion who loses the lane and wins the game, which is what the corrected chart now says.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 4 and 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs; ratings set to 5 for Skill, 3 for her rows, 7 for yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer claimed Level 6 and Liandry's as your spikes; Level 6 is hers and only 2+ items is yours.
audit.why: Between Worlds (140s at rank 1) zones a slice of lane, and The Weirding (15/14/13/12/11s) hops her backwards out of the drowsy delay. Your reclaim is the second item, where the percent-HP burn kills a champion with one escape.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Between Worlds and The Weirding; phases[6].why states the 2+ item reclaim.

audit.whatIsWrong: TWO real errors. (a) The page never names Twofold Hex, Across the Veil, The Weirding or Between Worlds — packet defect. (b) The content layer repeatedly calls her W 'untargetable'. Riot's text says she becomes INVISIBLE, which is a different thing entirely.
audit.why: Invisibility loses to reveals. Swirlseed carries revealsStealth, so rolling the seed at where she vanished reveals her AND slows her — the single decisive unstated interaction in this matchup, and the mirror recorded it from her side too. Separately, Lilting Lullaby only sleeps enemies who already carry Dream Dust, so a clean Aurora cannot be slept at all.
audit.corrected: Real names inserted across the level-chart whys; the invisible-not-untargetable correction and the Swirlseed reveal are now in phases[2].why, spikes[1].text and wants.foe[0]; the Dream Dust precondition is on wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d called Across the Veil a fifteen-second cooldown.
audit.why: It is 22/21/20/19/18 — the longest cooldown in her kit and the widest window you get.

edits.after: Both of you have one ability — farm the outer Q edge from max range and concede nothing to Twofold Hex.

edits.before: W sweetspot threat starts — anyone chasing you eats the big hit while your Dream Dust burns their HP bar.
edits.after: Her spike at 2 — Across the Veil turns her invisible and Twofold Hex out-pokes you before the burn stacks.

edits.after: Roll Swirlseed at her Across the Veil — it reveals the invisibility and slows her out of the poke pattern.

edits.after: Ranged versus melee — The Weirding at 15s hops her back out of every gap your stacking Q move speed just closed.

edits.after: Her first-item burst still out-pokes you — bait The Weirding first, then spend the kite chain on her.

edits.before: You're a teamfight nightmare now: sleep two, kite the rest, and let the burn do the bookkeeping.

edits.before: Aurora burns Across the Veil (Hop) on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Aurora burns Across the Veil on nothing — that is 22 seconds at rank 1, so go now.

edits.before: Aurora's spike: her W spirit-form gives untargetability and her Q chips you faster than your Dream Dust stacks here.
edits.after: Aurora's spike: Across the Veil hides her — invisible, not untargetable, so Swirlseed still reveals and slows her.

edits.before: Stack Dream Dust passive DoT in any trade so even a brief touch costs her HP over time
edits.after: Land Q or Swirlseed first — Lilting Lullaby only sleeps targets already carrying Dream Dust.

edits.before: Poke you with Q and stay untargetable in W spirit-form so your Dream Dust never sticks
edits.after: Poke with Twofold Hex and vanish in Across the Veil so your Dream Dust never sticks.

notes: Highest-value fix here is not the chart: the content layer taught the reader that Across the Veil makes Aurora UNTARGETABLE. Riot's text says invisible. That difference decides the matchup, because Swirlseed reveals stealth — the seed both finds her and slows her, and a player told 'untargetable' will never try it. Corrected in the three places it was stated; the phrase 'untargetability' may survive elsewhere in early/mid if it appears outside the fields I edited. Only 5 recorded games at Emerald+ so the 60% is noise, though the corrected chart (lose lane, win late) is consistent with a positive record. The full layer still uses he/his for Aurora throughout and calls her W 'Across the Veil (Hop)' with a parenthetical that is not part of the name — flagged for a naming pass, including focus.text which is what the loading screen shows.
